name: Shared caption contract
description: Fragments merged into every Ideogram caption. `forbidden_suffix` is what keeps text, lettering and creatures out of every map - Ideogram takes no negative prompt, so this sentence is the only thing enforcing it.
aesthetics: Hand-painted fantasy cartography, rough painterly brushwork with visible strokes, strong dark ink outlines around every object and wall, subtle black and brown linework, restrained desaturated colour, flat orthographic projection with every object drawn as its top surface and a short soft shadow cast beside it on the floor, inked line art over watercolour and gouache, premium hand-drawn D&D virtual tabletop map, dense environmental storytelling with many small props and clutter
medium: Inked line art combined with watercolour and gouache painting over digital texture
art_style: hand-painted fantasy cartography, inked line art over watercolour and gouache, flat orthographic top-down battle map
lighting: Soft warm ambient light from directly above with gentle directional shadows beneath walls and furniture
forbidden_suffix: The scene is completely empty of people, creatures and animals, and carries no text, letters, numbers, labels or grid lines anywhere
background_suffix: painted with visible brushwork, every part of the ground fully painted with no blank patches inside the map area
border_note: A plain flat unpainted margin runs right around the outside of the image on all four sides, empty of scenery, buildings, water and props: bare paper, one flat colour, nothing painted on it at all. The map itself sits wholly inside that margin, and at its outer edge the ground simply stops in a clean straight line - the last squares of floor, water or rock run right up to that line and end there, with no frame, no kerb, no border of stones, no edging and no decoration of any kind drawn round the map
viewpoint_note: The view is strictly orthographic and from directly overhead, square to the floor, as if photographed from a ladder straight above the middle of the map: every wall is seen as the flat top edge of that wall and never as its face, every object is seen as its top surface, nothing recedes, there is no horizon, no vanishing point, no perspective and no tilt. The roof of this place, and every floor that was above this one, have been lifted away and carried off before the picture was taken, so what is shown is this floor, the top edges of the walls and the top surfaces of the things standing on it, and above all of that is open sky. Nothing of the structure that carried them is left: no beam, no joist, no rafter and no timber frame stands anywhere in the picture. Every single thing in the picture rests on the floor or on something else that rests on it. The whole picture reads flat, like a printed battle map laid on a table
viewpoint_note_open: The view is strictly orthographic and from directly overhead, square to the ground, as if photographed from straight above the middle of the map: every object is seen as its top surface, every building is seen as the top edges of its outer walls, nothing recedes, there is no horizon, no vanishing point, no perspective and no tilt. This is an open-air outdoor site under open sky with no overhead cover. Nothing stands over the open ground. Every single thing in the picture rests on the ground or on a floor. The whole picture reads flat, like a printed battle map laid on a table
